messages:
anya: Quick thought — I want to prototype per-API-key priority buckets (high/normal/low) that influence routing + quota precedence + telemetry sampling. planning doc incoming but wanted quick feedback first. main goals: route high->low-latency pools, normal->balanced, low->cheap/quantized variants; sample telemetry aggressively for high, sparse for low. questions: 1) how should console expose/let users set buckets? 2) recommended default sampling ratios? 3) billing & quota implications?

mike: +1 to the idea. two immediate concerns: quota fairness (low-priority noisy tenants gaming cheaper path) and cost visibility — we need to show cost-per-bucket. also how does this interact with reserved capacity?

sam: we can piggyback on existing routing policy fields (route_preference) so minimal infra churn. console UX: default all existing keys to "normal" and add a bulk-edit for org admins. add a small badge on key detail: "Priority: high". metrics: add priority_breakdown and token_burn_by_priority.

jordan: for sampling ratios i'd start conservative. example: {"high": 1.0, "normal": 0.1, "low": 0.02}. that gives us full fidelity for high, cheap signals for low. rollout plan: start with internal-only flag, then opt-in customers, then default.

anya: @mike good call re reserved capacity — should high always bypass cheap pools when dedicated set? idea: routing policy precedence: 1) explicit route on key > 2) project-level override > 3) priority bucket default. anyone see holes?

mike: that precedence looks right. but also need a circuit-breaker: if high-latency pool saturates, we should optionally spill to normal (configurable). otherwise failing fast might be disruptive.

sam: console affordances: UI dropdown on key create/edit (High/Normal/Low), hover tooltip explaining cost/latency tradeoffs, and a little docs CTA linking to recommendations. add a server-side default that org admins can lock.

jordan: mapping rules sketch (pseudo):
```json
{
  "effective_priority": "key.priority || project.priority_override || 'normal'",
  "route_target": "route_table[effective_priority] || route_table['normal']"
}
```
This keeps inheritance simple.

anya: +1. also telemetry naming: suggest tag all traces/spans with priority_bucket and route_target so we can correlate latency/cost per bucket. Sam — can you add those fields to the existing tracing schema?

sam: yep. I'll add span tag "priority_bucket" and an analytic dimension "route_target". will also add an ingestion pipeline rule to sample differently by bucket.

mike: on billing: propose we do not change unit pricing initially — treat priority as routing+telemetry knob only. if customers want guaranteed low latency via dedicated pools we surface "dedicated reservation" upsell. but we should show projected cost delta in key edit UI (simulate expected unit cost).

anya: good plan. also need to update quota UI to show quota per-priority? maybe not per-key, but per-project we can show consumed by bucket to catch abuse. thoughts?

jordan: per-project breakdown is enough. per-key is noisy and rarely needed. add anomaly alerts if low-priority token suddenly consumes > X% of quota.

devex-bot: mockup uploaded: https://redwood-internal.mockups/priority-buckets/edy1 — includes edit modal + cost projection table.

anya: cool mock, thanks. one last ops ask: rollout playbook checklist? I'd propose: 1) feature flag + infra metric gates, 2) internal dogfood for 1 week, 3) opt-in beta customers, 4) monitor latency/cost delta and alerts, 5) gradual default flip. assign owners?

sam: I'll own console work + tags.

jordan: I'll own telemetry ingestion and alert rules.

mike: I'll own routing fallback logic and SLO updates.

anya: thanks all. I'll draft a short design doc and attach the mockup link + proposed sampling numbers. sync next Tues 10am if this looks ok. :thumbsup:
